name: Lake Tschida - Downstream Campground (Grant County)
note: Lake Tschida's camping area below Heart Butte Dam in the Heart River bottom, with a fishing pier on the stilling pond, picnic shelters at many sites, a playground and two rental cabins. Sites are open grass spots under cottonwoods marked by posts, with no pads. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: laketschida.org/downstream (BOR/JJDA per-site map) + downstream-electric-1/-2 (21 sites with posted amperage) and downstream-primitive (8 sites), Peek programs aKom/gVWOz selling single nights; operator photos show open grass sites on loop roads -> real drive-in RV campground. Separate from 6025 Rimrock: 1.27 km away on the downstream side of the dam, own loop road from ND 49. Operator Lake Tschida Recreation (Tri-Cities Joint Job Development Authority, the managing partner with the Bureau of Reclamation; same operator and ownership as 6025 Rimrock), laketschida.org read 2026-11-12. 'Camping unit' covers motor homes and pull-type campers (campground rules). Horse rule passes: the Hidden Shelter page says it is 'the only campground at Lake Tschida that will accommodate horses' and it is a separate area. Long-stay test 4: every site is sold by the night on Peek; the private cabin and trailer permittee areas are separate lease areas, not campground sites. Public (local): no price gate or presence rule.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12 dam check: Heart Butte Dam axis ~0.5 km W (OSM dam node 46.5963,-101.81018); the pads are downstream of it at 622 m DEM (Open-Meteo) against 627 m on the lake's open water (46.6000,-101.8300), so no lake value. Tailwater: the Heart River (~25-30 m wide here) runs SE of the loops; the official map puts the outer loop road between the river and sites 37, 43 and 51-54, and Esri World Imagery (1 km frame at 46.5965,-101.8050) shows a continuous tree belt along the north bank. Only primitive 19 sits on the river side of the main road, ~25 m from the bank under trees, and its photo shows no water -> not waterfront.

fees.note: Electric $24, primitive $14 a night; the two cabins are $45.

fees_source: https://laketschida.org/camping-fees ('$14 nightly fee for a primitive campsite at all campsites'; '$24 nightly fee for electrical campsites.'), read 2026-11-12 ('$45 nightly fee for the Downstream cabins.')
hookups_source: https://laketschida.org/downstream-electric-1 ('DOWNSTREAM ELECTRIC CAMPSITE 21 (50/30 Amp)', '... 22 (30 Amp)' ...) and -2 ('... 52 (50/30 Amp)'), read 2026-11-12

sites.note: Electric 21-24, 26, 31-37, 41-45 and 51-54 (11 of them 50 A, the rest 30 A); primitive 8-13, 19 and 30 (8-10 ADA). Grass sites, no pads.

sites_source: https://laketschida.org/downstream-electric-1, -2 and downstream-primitive site lists, the Downstream map and Peek photos, read 2026-11-12

booking.note: Online booking closes 7 days out; inside a week, book by phone with the office. Friday or Saturday arrivals must take two nights between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Unreserved sites are first come, first served with envelopes at the self-registration kiosks (cash or check).

booking_source: https://laketschida.org/campground-information ('7 DAY RULE ... If you want to make a reservation less than 7 days in advance you must call the office'; 'the minimum of 2 NIGHTS is required between Memorial Day weekend and Labor Day weekend'; 'No campsite may be occupied for more than 14 consecutive days out of 30 consecutive days'); https://laketschida.org/camping-fees ('camping envelopes are provided at self-registration Kiosks ... First Come First Serve'); https://laketschida.org/general-information ('all unreserved sites are available on a first come first serve basis'); the area's Peek booking program; read 2026-11-12
flags: 1.27 km from 6025 Rimrock (inside the 2 km check) but on the other side of the dam with its own road; not within 300 m, so no separate_from needed.
No pads: open grass sites with post markers (kept under the 2026-11-12 rule for designated points without pads).
No season is published for any Lake Tschida area.
curation_note: ND lead 9 (2026-11-12): below Heart Butte Dam; DEM 622 m vs 627 m lake, so judged on the Heart River only. --Claude
